newsitem.title: CHINA: China says Radio Free Asia has "shameful" mission.
newsitem.headline: China says Radio Free Asia has "shameful" mission.

text.p: China slammed a U.S.-funded radio station on Thursday, saying it had an "ugly face" and a "shameful mission" of inciting Asians to overthrow their governments.
The China Youth Daily fired the anti-U.S. salvo on the last day of a visit by U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher to China.
Radio Free Asia, created as a private corporation funded by the United States Congress, began Chinese-language broadcasts on September 29 and Tibetan programming on November 18.
"As soon as it (the radio station) appeared on stage, it showed its ugly face to the people," said the newspaper, published by the Communist Party's youth wing.
"The mission of the radio station is to incite Asian people to rise up and overthrow their own governments," it said.
The anti-communist station also broadcasts to Burma, Laos, Vietnam, Cambodia and North Korea.
It does not disclose the location of its transmitters to prevent jamming and avoid embarrassment to its hosts.
"Because the radio station has the shameful mission of overthrowing other governments, it is evasive in front of the world," said the newspaper.
China has accused the radio station of interfering in its internal affairs.
